label: Polished Businesses panel
title: A clearer view of work waiting to be done.
alt: Polished Businesses panel with zero of four operating businesses, compact terms, ready-to-appoint vacancy labels and readable Market and Dyers rows.
body: The polish pass wraps status text, fixes portrait sizes, highlights the selected sub-tab and makes space for a practical next step. Market and Dyers both say an operator is available in this campaign. Full appointment terms are available on hover.
note: Actual current-row rendering check. This capture predates the navigation-only bridge fix; it proves the visible layout, not Domain-button or alert click-through. The no-candidate test subsequently changed the labels to “no eligible household” and produced an empty native picker.

label: Domain Affluence tooltip
title: See how families feed the pillar.
alt: Domain Affluence tooltip showing household wealth in the baseline and a Households and businesses section with zero of four operating premises and one unassigned eligible household.
body: The Domain hover connects household assets to Affluence. It shows 0/4 operating premises and one unassigned eligible household, explains seasonal wealth growth and recommends staffing existing vacancies before building more.
note: This is the full Affluence-card hover. Its new text rendered without a tooltip error. The separate Quarter-driver hover and construction-advice scenario were not independently live-tested in this pass.

label: Household wealth
title: Families build wealth over time.
alt: Households panel showing HaLevi and Weil, Light assessment at 10 percent, and Weil wealth 39 out of 100.
body: The household panel separates family assets from a character’s personal purse. Here, Light assessment is selected and the Weil household has reached 39/100 wealth. Its displayed contribution is 0.04 gold per month, collected quarterly.
note: Historical UI: the four pooled assignment buttons were subsequently replaced by named business positions. The leading-family note clips in this capture; its wording was shortened afterward.

label: Business premises
title: A building needs an operating household.
alt: Businesses roster with zero of four businesses operating, including vacant Market and Dyers’ Workshop rows with zero operating income.
body: The Businesses tab lists built premises and their operating households. This campaign starts at 0/4 operating businesses. The vacant dyers’ workshop displays zero dyes and zero operating income.
note: Earlier revision: this capture exposed a disabled Appoint control and clipped text. Explicit native position bindings and narrower, wrapping rows were added before the final hire test.

label: Native appointment
title: Choose a Ba’al Bayit for the trade.
alt: Native Appoint Master Dyer picker containing Rav Yehonatan, Average aptitude, and a No Cost salary.
body: The corrected Appoint button opens CK3’s native picker. Rav Yehonatan is the one eligible candidate in this fresh campaign, with Average aptitude and No Cost. The household can hold one business job alongside a civic or religious office.
note: After this capture, selecting and confirming Rav Yehonatan immediately changed utilization to 1/4 and showed him as Master Dyer. The tester verified that before any diagnostic refresh. The post-hire desktop capture is omitted here because it includes unrelated windows.

label: Operating workshop
title: The operator brings the workshop to life.
alt: Staffed Dyers’ Workshop row with a Margolis operator portrait, Replace and Dismiss controls, one dye, and 0.10 monthly operating income.
body: An earlier campaign shows the staffed dyers’ workshop under the Margolis household: one dye of workshop output and 0.10 gold per month of business operating income. Replace and Dismiss are native position controls.
note: This is the scripted-hire campaign, not the later Rav Yehonatan campaign. Clipping in the row was subsequently addressed. Backend revocation returned workshop output and income to zero; manual dismissal and delivery into the native market remain unverified.
